oewn-07539144-n.learner: an unclear, unpleasant feeling you have because you expect that something bad is coming, though you may not know just what.
examples: His anxiety for Jane was evident, and his attentions to herself most pleasing.
Every day at Longbourn was now a day of anxiety.

oewn-14397837-n.learner: in psychiatry, a fairly lasting state of worry and nervousness that appears in many different mental disorders, usually along with compulsive behaviour or attacks of panic.
examples: Her anxiety was severe enough to be treated with therapy and medication.

oewn-00407168-v.learner: to make someone or something ready or fitting, or to supply what is needed, ahead of a certain purpose, use, or event.
examples: she was preparing to see him with a degree of composure which astonished her husband and daughters
"You shall hear, then--but prepare for something very dreadful."

oewn-01668067-v.learner: to make food ready to eat by putting heat to it.
examples: She prepared a hot supper of soup and bread.

oewn-01758079-v.learner: to put something together in words, either to be written down or to be spoken aloud.
examples: He prepared a short speech to give at the meeting.

oewn-01191258-v.learner: to have a need for something.
examples: He was too happy, however, to need much attention.

oewn-02634015-v.learner: to call for something because it is useful, right, or fitting.
examples: Mending the roof needs two people and a full day.

oewn-01191646-v.learner: to have a need for something, or to feel that you need it.
examples: After the long walk she needed a rest.

oewn-00307112-a.learner: having the ability or power for something; it is usually said with 'of'.
examples: You could not have met with a person more capable of giving you certain information on that head than myself.

oewn-00308813-a.learner: having the sort of nature or the leaning that would bring you to do something; it is said with 'of'.
examples: No man of common humanity, no man who had any value for his character, could be capable of it.
But of every other neglect I can believe him capable.

oewn-00512273-s.learner: having the skill and the training needed to do things well.
examples: She proved a capable nurse through the long illness.

connotation.why: praises the person as good at what they do

oewn-00101231-r.learner: at a point near the beginning of something.
examples: Early in the book, the family moves to a new town.

oewn-00100632-r.learner: before the usual time, or before the time people were expecting.
examples: the elder may not have the means or inclination to marry early

oewn-00101142-r.learner: soon enough, with time still to spare.
examples: Come early so that we get good seats.

oewn-00066148-r.learner: at the most recent time before now.
examples: Her thoughts were instantly driven back to the time when Mr. Bingley's name had been last mentioned between them.

oewn-00066222-r.learner: after everything else, as the item that comes at the end.
examples: Last, I want to thank everyone who helped.

oewn-02034003-v.learner: to move away from each other, each one going his or her own way.
examples: they parted on each side with the utmost politeness

oewn-02436167-v.learner: to end a connection or relationship with someone and go different ways.
examples: After ten years together, they parted for good.

oewn-02018017-v.learner: to leave in order to go somewhere.
examples: She parted for London the next morning.

oewn-00092442-v.learner: to get well again after an illness, or to get over a shock.
examples: when your sister is recovered, you shall, if you please, name the very day of the ball
She could not yet recover from the surprise of what had happened.

oewn-02252785-v.learner: to get something back or find it again, or to be able to use it again.
examples: The police recovered the stolen paintings.

oewn-02254246-v.learner: to win back what you lost, or to make up for it.
examples: He worked extra hours to recover the money he had lost.

oewn-81484980-r.learner: very quickly and with no warning.
examples: he suddenly recollected himself, and took leave
she turned suddenly towards him and said

oewn-02158938-v.learner: to see something with your eyes and so make out that it is there or that it is so.
examples: If I can perceive her regard for him, he must be a simpleton indeed not to discover it too.

oewn-01641524-v.learner: to find out something new that was not known before.
examples: I wonder who first discovered the efficacy of poetry in driving away love!

oewn-00600349-v.learner: to come to know something or become aware of it, usually by chance.
examples: our coincidence of feeling was soon discovered
They discovered that the house had once been a school.
